h1:
A Rainy-Season Fruit Plan
Chasing Langsat & Long Durian in Laplae
intro: Uttaradit is home to fruit you won't find quite the same anywhere else: Long Laplae and Lin Laplae durians, both GI-registered, and mountain-grown langsat and longkong planted up in the hills of Laplae. The fruit season here runs through the rains and into the late-rainy months. If you're the kind of traveler who wants to eat fruit right where it grows, here's a 3-day plan that takes you to real orchards in Laplae district, eating fresh under the trees and stopping at durian-orchard cafés along the way.

blocks.html: When locals talk about Laplae fruit, they think of two windows in a year. The first is durian, ripening roughly May to July. The second is langsat and longkong, ripening roughly September to November. Both fall in the rainy season, but they're a few months apart, so you'll want to pick the right window before you set off. This plan works for either season, you just swap which fruit gets to be the star.

items: Long & Lin Laplae durian — ripens around May–July. These are Laplae's GI varieties: dry-fleshed, mild in smell, sweet and creamy. You can barely find them at any other time of year.
Langsat — ripens around September–November. Thin skin, translucent flesh, sweet with a slight tang, small seeds. This is the fruit that put Laplae on the map long ago.
Mountain longkong — ripens alongside langsat, grown up in the Laplae hills. Firmer, drier flesh and a deeper flavor than lowland longkong, because it's grafted onto old langsat rootstock.
Fruit festival — during durian season there's usually an event at the central fruit market in Hua Dong, Laplae district (June–July), where orchards from across the district gather in one place.

blocks.title: Pick Your Season Before You Book
blocks.html: If you're coming for Long & Lin durian, aim for late May through July. If you want langsat and mountain longkong eaten straight at the orchard, push your trip to September–October. Fresh fruit at the orchard is far cheaper and fresher than buying it in town.

blocks.text: Orchards & Cafés Where You Can Eat at the Source

blocks.html: Laplae has turned several of its fruit orchards into places where you can sit and eat under the trees, with cafés set right in the groves, so you can get that orchard feel without hiking up the hills. These are the spots that actually open their gates to visitors to eat and take photos.

items.name: Long Suan Na Laplae
items.blurb: A café set inside a durian orchard, built as a glass pavilion ringed by greenery, with a wooden deck looking out over hills and forest. Sip a drink with something sweet, then buy durian and seasonal fruit to take home. An easy starting point if it's your first time here.

items.name: Suan Pa Rian (Summer Green)
items.blurb: A durian orchard that grew into a café for durian lovers, with seating in the middle of the grove, graded durian at a range of prices, and offbeat menu items like longkong toast, longkong sorbet, and longkong som tam. A fun place to see how Laplae fruit gets turned into other things.

items.name: Mon Laplae
items.blurb: A restaurant and café decorated in Lanna style within a shady garden, with a coffee zone, a food zone, and a corner selling processed-fruit souvenirs and local handicrafts. Good for a lunch stop before heading into the orchards.

items.name: Hua Dong Central Fruit Market
items.blurb: Where fruit from orchards across the district comes together. It's busiest in durian season, with Long, Lin and other varieties at orchard prices and plenty to choose from. Locals genuinely shop here, so you'll find fresh produce at good prices.
items.meta: Hua Dong, Laplae district · busiest in durian season

blocks.title: Getting Your Money's Worth on Durian
blocks.html: Orchards usually let you taste before you buy. Pick fruit with full, plump segments and a stem that's still fresh. If you can't finish it, ask them to package it in a chilled box. Long and Lin have dry flesh and keep in the fridge for a couple of days without going mushy.

You can base yourself in Uttaradit town or in Laplae district itself, since most orchards are in Laplae, about 8–10 km from town. Day one is easy, just getting to know the area. Day two goes all in on the orchards. The last day is for picking up souvenirs before you head home.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Into Town, Getting to Know Laplae

items.activity: Arrive in Uttaradit and have lunch at Mon Laplae
items.note: Local food in a shady garden, a good first taste of Laplae's cooking.

items.activity: Stop by the Phraya Phichai Dap Hak Monument, then pass through the Laplae city gate
items.note: Grab photos of the town's landmarks. The yellow Sukhothai-style gate is about 6 km from the monument.

items.activity: Relax at the café at Long Suan Na Laplae
items.note: A glass pavilion inside a durian orchard with hill views. Try a dessert made from whatever fruit is in season.

items.activity: Find a place to stay in town or in Laplae and have dinner in town
items.note: Staying near Laplae makes it easy to get to the orchards early.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: A Full Day in the Orchards, Eating at the Tree

items.activity: Head to the Hua Dong central fruit market
items.note: In durian season it's lively from early on. Pick Long and Lin from several orchards, and you can taste before you buy.

items.activity: Visit Suan Pa Rian (Summer Green) and eat in the grove
items.note: Try the processed-fruit menu, longkong toast and longkong som tam, and buy graded durian to take home.

items.activity: Have lunch around Laplae, then rest during the heat
items.note: Rainy season means sun and showers in turns, so build in time to wait out the afternoon rain.

items.activity: Go up to the Mon Laplae viewpoint or stroll the Laplae town market
items.note: If the rain isn't heavy, the hillside orchard views look lovely in the late-afternoon light.

items.activity: Head back to your room and chill the fruit you bought
items.note: Long and Lin have dry flesh and keep well in the fridge.

items.activity: Have a Laplae-style breakfast, then stop at a café for coffee to go
items.note: An easy start to the day before a long drive.

items.activity: Buy processed-fruit souvenirs at Mon Laplae or a souvenir shop in the market
items.note: Durian paste, dried langsat and longkong, and other processed fruit travel well.
If you want to keep traveling, Phrae and Sukhothai are close by and an easy drive on.

items: Your own car is easiest — the orchards are spread across Laplae district, about 8–10 km from town, and there's no public transport that runs right to them.
Pack an umbrella for the rains — fruit season is rainy season, with showers coming and going. Orchard ground gets slippery, so non-slip shoes help.
Hit the orchards in the morning — the fruit is fresher and there are fewer people than in the afternoon. In durian season the best fruit sells out fast.
Carry cash — many orchard stalls and markets are mainly cash-only.

items.name: Onward to Phrae
items.blurb: Not far to drive from Uttaradit, an old town of teak houses and cafés that pairs nicely as a next stop.

items.name: Onward to Sukhothai
items.blurb: The historical park is close by, a good way to end a culture-focused trip.

faq.q: Do Long Laplae durian and langsat ripen in the same month?
faq.a: No, they're in different windows. Long and Lin Laplae durian ripen around May to July, while langsat and mountain longkong ripen around September to November. If you want one of them to be the star, pick your travel month to match that window.

faq.q: Can you really eat fruit right at the orchard, and where?
faq.a: Yes. Laplae has orchards that let you sit and eat and have turned into cafés, such as Long Suan Na Laplae, Suan Pa Rian (Summer Green), and Mon Laplae. The Hua Dong central fruit market is where you buy fresh produce gathered from orchards across the district.

faq.q: What makes Long and Lin Laplae durian special?
faq.a: They're native Laplae varieties that are GI-registered. The flesh is fairly dry, the smell is mild, and the taste is sweet and creamy. They grow well only in this area, which is why they're hard to find elsewhere.

faq.q: What's the best way to get around the Laplae fruit orchards?
faq.a: Your own car is easiest, because the orchards are spread across Laplae district about 8–10 km from town, and there's no public transport running directly to them.

faq.q: Is visiting orchards in the rainy season a hassle?
faq.a: It's doable, but rain comes in spells and the orchard ground can get slippery. Bring an umbrella, wear non-slip shoes, and go in the morning, when it usually hasn't started raining yet and the fruit is fresher.
